context:
Each cluster gets its own commit (or small commit series). Start with
w1 and w5 - lowest-risk, highest-density wins.

w1 (_safe_metadata_collect): a trivial wrapper - the risk is only that
some call sites catch a *specific* exception today. Audit each try
block before migrating; preserve specificity where it exists.

w5 (pricing dict dispatch): mirror bigquery._determine_bigquery_pricing.
Key design choice: fall through to a DEFAULT_PRICING_PLAN entry rather
than returning None, to match current behavior.

w2 (credential_setup_flow): design the field-schema dataclass first;
migrate athena first since it has the cleanest shape (already refactored
for C901 in commit 3288e108f). Validator stays per-platform.

w3 (catalog loader): spec object per benchmark family; single loader
parses YAML/JSON and produces SchemaCollection. Preserve per-benchmark
quirks as spec-level flags, not branches in the loader.

w4 (ServiceLimitCollector): Protocol + dispatch registry. Start with
EC2 (most complex) to surface interface requirements, then port the
simpler services.
description:
Follow-up to quality-consolidate-duplicate-code-clusters. The C901
complexity-reduction grind (quality-reduce-complexity-hotspots-to-mccabe-20)
has surfaced 5 additional duplicate-code clusters that are prime targets
for shared helpers. Consolidating them removes ~200-300 LOC, reduces
maintenance surface when adding new cloud adapters / benchmark families,
and eliminates a common C901 contributor (the try/except-per-metadata-call
shape and long if/elif commitment-plan ladders).

Dependency note: w1 and w5 are independent and lowest-risk - start there.
w2 touches interactive code paths and should be done after w1 (same
adapters). w3 and w4 are independent of the rest.

Clusters identified:

1. Platform `get_platform_info` scaffolding
   Files: benchbox/platforms/bigquery.py, snowflake.py, databricks/*.py,
          redshift.py, athena.py (and clickhouse/metadata.py)
   Pattern: Each cloud adapter repeats a try: value = fetch_metadata();
            except Exception: value = None block per metadata call.
   Proposed fix: Extract _safe_metadata_collect(name, fn) -> Any | None
            in benchbox/platforms/_platform_info_utils.py.
   Impact: ~80+ lines removed across 5+ files; side effect: reduces
            C901 complexity on get_platform_info methods.

2. setup_*_credentials interactive flows
   Files: benchbox/platforms/credentials/athena.py, bigquery.py,
          Azure/GCP equivalents
   Pattern: Each repeats env-var → existing-credentials-file → keyring →
            interactive-prompt chain + auto-detect + validate + save-next-
            steps section.
   Proposed fix: credential_setup_flow(platform, fields, auto_detector,
            validator) in benchbox/platforms/credentials/_flow.py; per-
            platform modules keep only field schema + validator.
   Impact: dedupe the auto-detect/prompt/finalize scaffolding today's
            athena C901 refactor surfaced (commit 3288e108f).

3. Catalog-loader shape (TPC-H vs TPC-DS)
   Files: benchbox/core/tpch/* and benchbox/core/tpcds/* -
          _load_*_schema / _load_*_catalog pairs
   Pattern: Same file-open → parse → validate → index shape, only
            benchmark-specific field names differ.
   Proposed fix: Parameterize over schema definitions; single
            load_catalog(schema_path, spec) with per-benchmark spec object.
   Impact: Lower maintenance cost when adding a new benchmark family
            (e.g., TPC-DI follow-ons).

4. aws_cost_limits.py per-service collectors
   Files: benchbox/platforms/_aws/aws_cost_limits.py (or equivalent)
   Pattern: EC2, S3, Redshift, Athena each duplicate the budget/limit
            fetch shape (client → describe → normalize → aggregate).
   Proposed fix: ServiceLimitCollector protocol + shared dispatch loop;
            per-service code becomes a short callable returning
            normalized records.
   Impact: Adding a new AWS service ~20 lines instead of ~80.

5. Pricing / commitment if/elif ladders → dict dispatch
   Files: benchbox/platforms/bigquery.py (already refactored this session
          via commitment_plan_map, commit 07cea9852), databricks/*.py,
          redshift.py
   Pattern: Long if plan == "x": ...; elif plan == "y": ... chains
            mapping commitment/edition strings to pricing model fields.
   Proposed fix: Module-level PRICING_PLAN_MAP: dict[str, tuple[
            pricing_model, edition]] + single .get() lookup - mirrors
            bigquery _determine_bigquery_pricing pattern.
   Impact: Removes ~30-50 lines per adapter; also removes a common
            C901 contributor.

anti_patterns.dont: bundle w1 + w2 + w3 into one commit
anti_patterns.instead: one commit per work unit minimum
if a call site differs, preserve the difference via a helper parameter

anti_patterns.dont: collapse _safe_metadata_collect blocks that catch specific exceptions
introduce a shared helper without at least 3 call sites
anti_patterns.instead: keep duplicated code if only 2 adapters use it

preserves.behavior: Catalog-load output shape (column names, types, row ordering) is byte-identical per benchmark
Existing behavior when metadata fetches fail (None → surfaced as None, not raised)
Interactive credential prompt sequence and error messages remain identical to the user
Pricing dict-lookup must fall back to current default when plan string is unknown
Public method signatures of get_platform_info, setup_*_credentials, catalog-loader entry points

scope_rules.path_glob: benchmark runners, query generators, result schema
files listed in the 5 clusters above

work_units.notes: Audited per-adapter try/except blocks. Exception handlers vary significantly: different exception types (ImportError/AttributeError vs broad Exception), multi-key mutations, cursor cleanup, conditional None guards. A bare _safe_metadata_collect(fn) would be lossy. Anti-pattern rule: not worthwhile with less than 3 identical call sites. Skipping.
work_units.summary: Extract _safe_metadata_collect helper in platforms/_platform_info_utils.py; migrate bigquery, snowflake, databricks, redshift, athena, clickhouse get_platform_info methods. Own commit per adapter.

work_units.notes: w1 was not warranted; w2 depends on w1. Also re-audited credential flows: athena and bigquery were heavily refactored for C901 already (commits 3288e108f, c7fdf9de6). The remaining differences (field schemas, validators, auto-detect logic) are platform-specific enough that a shared scaffold would paper over meaningful distinctions. Skipping.
work_units.summary: Extract credential_setup_flow scaffolding in platforms/credentials/_flow.py; migrate athena + bigquery + one Azure/GCP to prove the pattern. Keep per-platform field schemas and validators local.

work_units.notes: Audited benchbox/core/tpch/schema.py and benchbox/core/tpcds/schema/tables.py - structurally different, no shared _load_*_schema/_load_*_catalog pattern exists. The write_primitives and ai_primitives catalog loaders do share a _load_catalog_payload() shape, but core/primitives/catalog/loader.py already provides a parameterized shared loader for that family. Skipping.
work_units.summary: Parameterize catalog loaders; collapse TPC-H / TPC-DS _load_*_schema pairs into a single load_catalog(path, spec) function with per-benchmark spec objects.

work_units.notes: No aws_cost_limits.py file exists in the codebase. The AWS platform adapters (athena_spark, emr_serverless, glue) each set billing_model as a static string - no collect/describe/aggregate loop to unify. Skipping.
work_units.summary: Define ServiceLimitCollector protocol in aws_cost_limits; migrate EC2/S3/Redshift/Athena collectors to conform. Per-service code becomes normalized-record callables.

work_units.notes: Audited databricks/adapter.py and redshift.py - no pricing/commitment if-elif ladders exist. Only bigquery had this pattern; it was resolved in commit 07cea9852. w5 is complete by virtue of there being nothing to do.
work_units.summary: Convert pricing/commitment if-elif ladders in databricks + redshift to dict-dispatch tables (bigquery already done - use _determine_bigquery_pricing as reference). Own commit per adapter.
